The Krishi Robot, displayed at the Krishi Mela in Bengaluru. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
Krishi Robot, an agricuture advisory device, has been the centre of attraction at the ongoing Krishi Mela in Bengaluru.
It has been developed by the Centre of Excellence on Watershed Management at the University of Agriculture Sciences, Bengaluru. The institute claims that this robot is a first of its kind in India. Pruthviraj N., an agronomist involved in the development of the robot, said, “Krishi Robot is a village-level advisory device that scans Land Resource Inventory (LRI) cards to provide farmers with soil fertility details and crop-specific fertilizer recommendations without needing a smartphone or manual data entry.”
It has been developed to make scientific agricultural advice more accessible to farmers without them having to spend a single penny. These LRI cards are issued by the government after the farmer’s land is surveyed. Farmers can show the LRI cards to the robot, which scans the cards and provides detailed reports on the properties of the soil and nutrients present in it, Mr. Pruthviraj said.
Through voice-based interactions in Kannada, it also provides recommendations related to fertilizers to be used for specific crops. Besides, the robot has been designed in a way that if farmers display a leaf in front of the robot, it scans and provides details of the leaf. Other details including diseases on the crop, its intensity and other factors are also displayed.
“The robot can provide information about 128 crops. A WiFi connection is a must for the robot to function. In the future, we are likely to place this robot at Farmers’ Outreach Centres of Raita Samparka Kendras. It aims to address digital literacy gap as most farmers in remote areas might not know or understand how to use applications on smartphones,” Mr. Pruthviraj said.
